text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for /api/v1/generate in prod cluster us-west-2. Canary (canary-42) error rate = 12% over 5m. Deploy at 13:07 UTC matched to pipeline run 2026-03-15T13:06Z. Paging eng-oncall.

alice (eng-oncall): I'm on it. Canary started failing ~13:10. Not seeing obvious runtime OOMs. Logs show a stacktrace in model-loader complaining about 'model metadata mismatch'.

mike (eng-infra): grabbing CI info now. Which image tag was deployed in canary?

sara (release-engineer): The rollout used tag redwood/model-serving:latest from the pipeline job. The job was supposed to retag with the commit SHA but the retag step failed silently in the last stage. I just pulled the pipeline run logs.

mike (eng-infra): Ok that's suspicious — we had a recent change that updated the retag helper. Grep from the registry: `curl -s https://registry.redwood.internal/v2/model-serving/tags/list | jq .tags` shows ["latest","sha-abc123","sha-old456"]. The canary points to `latest`.

alice (eng-oncall): Can you dump the image digest for 'latest' and for sha-old456? We need to know if latest got swapped under the hood (cache/retagging) or if the build itself produced a bad artifact.

mike (eng-infra): `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.internal/model-serving:latest | jq .Digest` -> sha256:deadbeef111
`skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.internal/model-serving:sha-old456 | jq .Digest` -> sha256:abcabcabc

mike (eng-infra): Those are different. Looks like latest was pushed after the canary tag decision. There's a race: the promotion job allowed 'latest' to be overwritten while other stages read tags from the manifest producer instead of pinned digests.

kevin (sre): Customer impact check: I see nginx upstream 5xx spikes around 13:10 for the canary shard only, but LB surfaced ~8% error rate across a small subset of users routed to canary. Dave, any customer tickets?

dave (product-support): Yes, we have 3 high-priority reports from customers using streaming endpoints. Messages: "partial stream then 500". One is on enterprise plan, opened at 13:15 UTC. Will update customers once we have mitigation.

alice (eng-oncall): Mitigation strategy: block further traffic to canary and rollback canary to previous pinned digest (sha-old456). If that's quick, then we can avoid full rollback. Sara — can you trigger canary kill-switch or route weight change?

sara (release-engineer): On it. Using redwoodctl to change route weight and pin digest. Commands:

```
# reduce canary traffic to 0%
redwoodctl routing set-weight --service model-serving --shard canary-42 --weight 0
# pin the running revision to the previous digest
redwoodctl deploy pin --service model-serving --shard canary-42 --image-digest sha256:abcabcabc
# roll forward the canary to pinned digest
redwoodctl deploy rollout --service model-serving --shard canary-42 --from-digest sha256:abcabcabc
```

sara (release-engineer): Sent the requests. API returned 202 for the weight change and rollout. Watching status.

mike (eng-infra): While that's happening, I'm opening the registry audit: looks like a scheduled promotion job retriggered and pushed 'latest' after an earlier successful build. The helper script didn't include `--no-overwrite` and the pipeline secret rotation coincided. Root cause candidate: retag helper allowed overwrite and the pipeline concurrency window allowed two pushes.

kevin (sre): Alice — after weight 0, confirm traffic is cut and 5xx rate goes down before we consider wider rollback. Also let's not flip global feature flags until we confirm rollback success.

alice (eng-oncall): Weight is at 0% now. LB shows all new requests going to stable. 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 2 minutes on the impacted endpoints in prod. :thumbsup:

dave (product-support): Notifying the three customers: one enterprise customer already acknowledged and is on a call. I'll file a customer-impact note in Zendesk and link to this thread.

sara (release-engineer): Canary now running pinned digest sha-old456. Health checks green. Smoke tests pass (local generation + streaming tests).

kevin (sre): Can we confirm that the pinned stable digest corresponds to the commit that passed nightly tests? We should cross-check artifact signature.

mike (eng-infra): Verified: registry artifact sha256:abcabcabc has signature from the signing key used last week and matches the build id 2026-03-14T22:05Z. That's the expected good build.

alice (eng-oncall): Great. I'll leave the canary pinned and keep traffic at 0% while we triage pipeline. Sara, can you do a quick rollback of the production pool if the investigation surfaces more affected clusters? For now production more broadly didn't see elevated errors.

sara (release-engineer): Will coordinate. No full prod rollback required at this time.

mike (eng-infra): Immediate remediation steps I'm taking:
- Add `--no-overwrite` to retag helper and force manifest pinning.
- Add a gating check in pipeline to verify digest equality after retag.
- Add a lock to promotion job to prevent concurrent pushes.

kevin (sre): Also add an alert for `image_digest_mismatch` when the deployed tag digest != pinned digest in manifests. That would've caught this earlier.

dave (product-support): I'm drafting a short customer update: root cause 'CI promotion allowed latest to be overwritten causing canary to pick up an unintended build. Mitigation applied: canary reverted to known-good digest; fix in CI started.'

alice (eng-oncall): Handoff: I'm paged and will remain on call for another hour. Sara and Mike will own the CI fix. Kevin will track alerts. Dave will own customer comms. We'll do a postmortem tomorrow and a change to require digest pinning in release playbook.

sara (release-engineer): Quick action items:
- PR to retag helper for --no-overwrite (mike)
- Pipeline gating check + e2e in canary context (sara)
- Add image_digest_mismatch alert (kevin)
- Postmortem + timeline draft (alice)

mike (eng-infra): PR opened: https://phab.redwood.org/D1234 — includes manifest locking and `--no-overwrite`. Running canary on staging with new helper.

alice (eng-oncall): Closing rotation: service stable, canary pinned at good digest, customer notify in progress. Leaving thread open for final postmortem link and followups. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved by configuration change and canary rollback at 13:22 UTC. Severity: S2. Log: `action=rollback canary=canary-42 digest=sha256:abcabcabc initiated_by=sara`

sara (release-engineer): Note for postmortem: add a step to avoid using mutable tags in release manifests and require digest-based manifests for any rollout automation.

kevin (sre): I'm adding the follow-up ticket to the oncall board and scheduling a review with CI owners.

alice (eng-oncall): Thanks team. If no objections I'll convert this into a postmortem draft tomorrow and link here.

dave (product-support): Thanks — customers updated. I'll paste the zendesk ticket ids in the postmortem.

sara (release-engineer): closing thread when PM approves postmortem content.
